triples.source_text: The king answered Daniel, who was called Baltasar in Chaldean, “Will you be able to disclose to me the vision I saw and its interpretation?”

target_units.text: The chief eunuch assigned them names: Daniel, Baltasar; Hananiah, Sedrach; Mishael, Misach; and Azariah, Abdenago.

triples.rationale: Daniel denies that the court's specialists can disclose the king's mystery. Pharaoh's interpreters and wise men likewise fail to explain his dream before Joseph is summoned.

target_units.text: And morning came, and his soul was troubled; and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh told them the dream, and there was none to explain it to Pharaoh.

triples.rationale: Daniel says God has made known to the king what is to come. Joseph likewise explains that God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do, treating the royal dream as divine disclosure.

target_units.text: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh’s dream is one. God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
“The seven fair cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years. Pharaoh’s dream is one.
“And the seven lean cows which came up after them are seven years; and the seven thin ears, blighted by the wind, shall be seven years of famine.
“And this is the word which I have spoken to Pharaoh: God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.

triples.rationale: Daniel says the reclining king saw what must happen in the last days and that the Revealer disclosed the coming events. Joseph likewise says God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do, treating the royal dream as divine disclosure.
triples.source_text: You, O king, reclining upon your bed, saw everything that must happen in the last days, and the Revealer of mysteries disclosed to you what must happen.

triples.rationale: Daniel denies that the mystery was revealed because he possesses superior wisdom. Joseph similarly refuses to locate the saving answer in himself apart from God.
triples.source_text: This mystery was revealed to me because of no wisdom in me beyond all people; rather, so that it might be disclosed to the king, what you conceived in your heart was made known to me.

target_units.text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “Without God, no answer bringing deliverance shall be given to Pharaoh.”

triples.rationale: The impressive statue introduced in the dream becomes the subject of Daniel's announced interpretation, which identifies its successive materials with royal powers. The connection follows the account's own explanation of its image.
triples.source_text: You, O king, saw a single image. That image was exceedingly large, its appearance was extraordinary as it stood before you, and the image’s appearance was frightening.

target_units.text: This was the vision; now we will state its interpretation before the king.
You, O king, are king of kings, and the Lord of heaven has given you rule, kingdom, strength, honor, and glory.
Throughout the inhabited world He has handed over into your hands human beings, wild beasts, birds of heaven, and fish of the sea, to rule them all. You are the golden head.
After you a kingdom lesser than you will arise, and another, a third kingdom of bronze, which will rule the whole earth.
A fourth kingdom will be strong like iron that subdues everything and cuts down every tree, and the whole earth will be shaken.
As you saw its feet partly potter’s earthenware and partly iron, another kingdom, divided in two, will be within it, just as you saw iron mixed with clay earthenware.
The toes of the feet were partly iron and partly earthenware; part of the kingdom will be strong and part shattered.
As you saw iron mixed with clay earthenware, they will be mingled in human generation, but will neither agree nor have goodwill toward one another, just as iron cannot blend with earthenware.

triples.rationale: The statue's gold head, silver chest and arms, and bronze lower body are explained as the king and succeeding kingdoms. The explanation follows the same sequence of materials.

triples.relationship: divine grant and withdrawal of kingship
triples.rationale: Daniel attributes Nebuchadnezzar's kingship and power to the God of heaven. The later heavenly sentence removes his kingdom and declares that God gives human kingship to whomever He wishes.
triples.source_text: You, O king, are king of kings, and the Lord of heaven has given you rule, kingdom, strength, honor, and glory.

target_units.text: At the completion of his word, he heard a voice from heaven: “To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: Babylon’s kingdom has been taken from you and is given to another, a despised man in your house. Behold! I appoint him over your kingdom; he will take your authority, glory, and luxury, so that you may recognize that the God of heaven has authority over human kingship and will give it to whomever He wishes. By sunrise another king will rejoice in your house and take possession of your glory, strength, and authority.

triples.rationale: The gold head is identified with Nebuchadnezzar's extensive dominion over living creatures; the later tree vision also identifies its great, sheltering image with the king and the peoples serving him.
triples.source_text: Throughout the inhabited world He has handed over into your hands human beings, wild beasts, birds of heaven, and fish of the sea, to rule them all. You are the golden head.

target_units.text: You, O king, are the tree planted in the earth, whose appearance was great.
And all the birds of heaven nesting in it—the strength of the earth and of the nations and of all languages to the ends of the earth, and all countries—serve you.

The raising of that tree, its reaching heaven, and its mass touching the clouds mean that you, O king, were raised above all people upon the face of the whole earth. Your heart was raised in pride and strength against the Holy One and His angels. Your deeds were seen, because you laid waste the house of the living God on account of the sins of the consecrated people.

triples.relationship: narrative contrast in response to divine help
triples.rationale: Nebuchadnezzar orders sacrifices and libations to Daniel after prostrating himself before him. At Lystra the priest and crowd likewise propose sacrifices to human messengers. Acts explicitly records the apostles' refusal; Daniel's response to the ordered honors is not reported here.
triples.source_text: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell face down on the ground and prostrated himself before Daniel. He ordered sacrifices and libations made to him.

target_units.text: The priest of Zeus, whose shrine was before the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates and wanted to offer sacrifice with the crowds.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out

and saying, “Men, why are you doing these things? We too are human beings, of the same nature as you. We proclaim good news to you: turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them.

triples.rationale: Nebuchadnezzar acknowledges Daniel's God as God of gods and Lord of kings. His later thanksgiving again uses the titles God of gods, Lord of lords and King of kings after another demonstration of divine authority.
triples.source_text: The king spoke aloud to Daniel, “Truly your God is God of gods and Lord of kings, the One who alone brings hidden mysteries to light, because you have been able to disclose this mystery.”

target_units.text: I give thanks to the Most High and praise Him who created heaven and earth, seas and rivers, and everything in them. I give thanks and praise, for He is God of gods, Lord of lords, and King of kings. He performs signs and wonders and changes seasons and times, taking kingdoms from kings and appointing others in their place.

triples.rationale: The gifts and authority conferred on Daniel fulfill the king's earlier promise of rewards and honor for making known the dream and its interpretation.
